claims: C1 the example presents an ambiguous task from a developer
C2 the GOOD assistant translates the Python code to JavaScript without asking about the runtime environment
C3 the BAD assistant asks what runtime environment will be used
C4 the example demonstrates that a clarifying question is avoided by default for an ambiguous developer task

concepts.name: clarifying_question
concepts.gloss: Q is a question the assistant asks to clarify an ambiguous or underspecified aspect of the task
concepts.inference: the example's BAD assistant asks what runtime environment will be used; the concept of a clarifying question is needed to express the example's lesson

concepts.name: ambiguous_task
concepts.gloss: T is a task that is ambiguous or underspecified, so that a clarifying question could be asked about it
concepts.inference: the example's heading calls the task ambiguous; the concept is needed to express the example's lesson

concepts.name: developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the developer authority level
concepts.inference: the example's developer message is an instruction from the developer; the NEEDS contract and the shared-name signature assign this meaning

concepts.name: task_instruction
concepts.gloss: instruction I directs the assistant to perform task T
concepts.inference: the example's developer instruction directs translating the quoted code; the relation between an instruction and the task it directs is needed

concepts.name: ask_clarifying_questions_section_guideline_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule in the #ask_clarifying_questions section, which carries guideline authority
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; the node's example is presented under that section's guidance

concepts.name: rule_governing_act
concepts.gloss: rule R governs the act of asking a clarifying question
concepts.inference: the section's guideline authority is relevant to the act of asking a clarifying question; the relation between the rule and the act is needed

asserts.read_back: asking a clarifying question % is dispreferred when the task % is ambiguous and the instruction % comes from a developer, because the #ask_clarifying_questions section's guideline authority makes such questions a fallback rather than a default
asserts.body: ambiguous_task(T), developer_instruction(I), task_instruction(I, T), ask_clarifying_questions_section_guideline_authority(R), rule_governing_act(R, ask_clarifying_question), clarifying_question(Q)

closure.reason: the example shows a clarifying question being avoided by default, but it does not forbid asking one; it only marks asking as dispreferred, so silence leaves asking permitted
